subject: Compiler directives
notes: §7.3.4 GR3 'The state of compiler directives may be saved and restored with PUSH and POP directives. A 'stack' is maintained that the state of a directive may be pushed on to. A subsequent POP directive removes the item from the stack and restores the state of the directive to that when it was pushed.' (cite.py --check 7.3.4 OK). PB941 (landed) gave PUSH/POP state semantics: DirectiveStateStack per stage with carriers registered by DirectiveStateRegistry, the pushable set derived from the catalog. Probes: PP1 named PUSH/POP DEFINE restores VV=1; PP2 PUSH ALL/POP ALL restores; PT1/PT2 PUSH/POP TURN restores ON (abnormal termination on 1/0) and OFF (continues); PP3/PP8 depth-2 nesting pops 3->2->1 in LIFO order; PP4/PP6 the GR3 NOTE's case - a copybook that does PUSH DEFINE / DEFINE 9 / POP DEFINE leaves VV=1 for the text after the COPY; PP9 an extra POP is unsuccessful (COBOL2297 warning, DOC-A.1-140) and restores nothing. kb/Work PB1066 (open: the implicit POP ALL before END-PERFORM, §14.9.28.4 GR14, does not reach >>DEFINE) is a §7.3.22.4 / §14.9.28 residue, not this general stack rule. The golden derives its expected output from §7.3.22.4 GR1-3 and §7.3.20.4 GR1-3. || editions (adjudicator): 2023 only (PUSH and POP added by ISO/IEC 1989:2023 - Annex E.3.3 item 38; E.2 item 5 lists POP and PUSH as added compiler-directive words); COBOL0900 below 2023
